newsitem.title: CANADA: Teck's hopes rise for shot at Bre-X.
newsitem.headline: Teck's hopes rise for shot at Bre-X.

text.p: Teck Corp is growing more hopeful it will get a chance to propose a deal for Bre-X Minerals Ltd and its rich Busang gold discovery, Teck president Norman Keevil said Wednesday.
"We've been waiting in the hope it (the process) would get opened up and my guess is it will," Keevil told Reuters.

Placer Dome Inc announced a US$5 billion merger offer for Bre-X on Tuesday, saying it sensed the Indonesian government might be willing to consider other deals beside the joint venture being negotiated by Barrick Gold Corp.

Keevil agreed, saying that indications were mounting that more bids might be allowed. "I'm not sure any of us have any definitive feel for what is going on (in Indonesia), but there does seem to be a growing sense that this thing should be dealt with in an open process," he said.

Placer chief executive John Willson said Tuesday a bidding war would likely ensue for Bre-X if the Indonesian government allowed an open competition. He said he knew of at least four other companies who would be interested.
Teck and Newmont Mining Corp held talks with Bre-X before Indonesia directed it to negotiate a deal with Barrick.
Teck has not decided on its next step yet. "We'll sit back and wait and see what happens for a little while," Keevil said.
He declined to discuss the type of deal Teck might pursue but said a joint venture was clearly an option. Teck does not have the resources to attempt a solo deal with Bre-X, analysts have said.
"Most of our operations are joint ventures so we're very comfortable with that kind of concept," Keevil said when asked if working with others like Placer or Newmont might be an alternative.
Analysts have also named Freeport-McMoRan Copper & Gold Inc and Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd as potential suitors.
Barrick has said its deal with Bre-X stands despite Placer's stock offer. Bre-X and Barrick have not disclosed terms of their joint venture.

Teck would be unable to propose a merger like Placer did because it would not be entitled to use pooling-of-interests accounting, which has tax advantages, Keevil said. A pooling of interests is only allowed when the companies are of roughly similar size and there would be no change in control.

Teck's market capitalization of about C$2.9 billion is dwarfed by Bre-X's size of around C$5.3 billion. Moreover, because Keevil has about 30 percent voting control of Teck, a merger would trigger a change in control.
